claim: Keys in a custom key store cannot be rotated automatically; you rotate them manually by creating new keys and re-mapping the KMS aliases your application uses.
question: How do you rotate keys in a CloudHSM custom key store?

evidence.quote: The ability to automatically rotate key material in an AWS KMS custom key store is not supported.
Key rotation must be performed manually by creating new keys and re-mapping AWS KMS key aliases used by your application code to use the new keys for future encryption operations.

note: d056. Conflict to note: the XKS section of the same FAQ says automatic rotation is possible with XKS keys (inside the external key manager).

claim: AWS KMS does not need exclusive access to your CloudHSM cluster, so the cluster can also serve other applications, though heavy load on either side can reduce throughput for the other.
question: Can a CloudHSM cluster that backs a KMS key store also serve other applications?

evidence.quote: Yes, AWS KMS does not require exclusive access to your CloudHSM cluster.
However, if your cluster is supporting high, non-AWS KMS, workloads you may experience reduced throughput for operations using KMS keys in your custom key store.

claim: An external key store (XKS) is a custom key store backed by key management infrastructure that you own and manage outside AWS; all encryption and decryption with its KMS keys run in your key manager.
question: What is a KMS external key store?

evidence.quote: An external key store is a custom key store backed by an external key management infrastructure that you own and manage outside of AWS.

All encryption or decryption operations that use a KMS key in an external key store are performed in your key manager with cryptographic keys and operations that are under your control and are physically inaccessible to AWS.

claim: Use an external key store when rules or regulations require encryption keys to be stored and used outside AWS under your control.
question: When would you use a KMS external key store?

values.display: stored and used outside of AWS under your control

evidence.quote: XKS can help you comply with rules or regulations that require encryption keys to be stored and used outside of AWS under your control.

claim: AWS KMS forwards XKS requests to a component in your network called an XKS Proxy, which passes them to your key management infrastructure.
question: How does AWS KMS reach an external key manager?

evidence.quote: Requests to AWS KMS from integrated AWS services on your behalf or from your own applications are forwarded to a component in your network called an XKS Proxy.

claim: External keys support the symmetric encryption operations Encrypt, ReEncrypt, Decrypt and GenerateDataKey.
question: Which KMS operations work with external (XKS) keys?

evidence.quote: External keys support the following symmetric encryption operations: Encrypt, ReEncrypt, Decrypt, and GenerateDataKey.

claim: XKS keys can encrypt data in any AWS service that integrates with AWS KMS using customer managed keys.
question: Can AWS services use XKS keys?

values.display: any AWS service that integrates with AWS KMS

evidence.quote: You can use XKS keys to encrypt data in any AWS service that integrates with AWS KMS using customer managed keys.

claim: With XKS, data keys are double encrypted, first by a KMS key in AWS KMS and then by the key in your external key manager, so no ciphertext can be decrypted without the external key material.
question: What does double encryption guarantee for XKS keys?

values.display: no ciphertext can ever be decrypted

evidence.quote: This encrypted data key is then forwarded to your XKS Proxy implementation connected to your external key manager to be encrypted a second time under the key you define in your external key manager.
Double encryption provides the security control that no ciphertext can ever be decrypted without using the key material in your external key manager.

claim: XKS keys also work in your own applications with client-side symmetric encryption that uses AWS KMS as its key provider, such as the AWS Encryption SDK, the S3 Encryption Client and the DynamoDB Encryption Client.
question: Can XKS keys be used for client-side encryption?

values.display: XKS keys can also be used from within your own applications

evidence.quote: XKS keys can also be used from within your own applications when using a client-side symmetric encryption solution that uses AWS KMS as its key provider.
AWS open source client-side encryption solutions like the AWS Encryption SDK, S3 Encryption Client and DynamoDB Encryption Client support XKS keys.

claim: Existing KMS keys cannot be migrated into XKS keys; every XKS key must be created as a new KMS key, though existing data can be re-encrypted under new XKS keys.
question: Can existing KMS keys be converted to external key store keys?

values.display: You cannot migrate existing KMS keys
created as new keys in KMS

evidence.quote: All XKS keys must be created as new keys in KMS.
You cannot migrate existing KMS keys into XKS keys hosted in your external key manager.
You can re-encrypt existing data under newly generated XKS keys, assuming the AWS service or your own application supports the action.

claim: Like all customer managed keys, XKS keys cost $1 per month per key until they are deleted, and their requests are charged at the same rate as other symmetric KMS keys.
question: How much does an XKS key cost in AWS KMS?

evidence.quote: Like all customer managed keys, XKS keys are priced at $1 per month per key until they are deleted.
Requests under XKS keys are charged at the same rate as any other AWS KMS symmetric key.

note: Prices change; numbers lens should check against www/kms/pricing.

claim: Automatic rotation of XKS keys is possible but happens entirely in the external key manager; it is supported by the XKS specification and offered by most XKS vendors.
question: Can XKS keys be rotated automatically?

values.display: occurs entirely in the external key manager

evidence.quote: Automatic key rotation is supported by the XKS specification, and it is a capability provided by most vendors that support XKS.
Automatic rotation for XKS keys occurs entirely in the external key manager and works in a similar way to the automatic key rotation for AWS KMS keys created and managed within KMS.

note: d056. Not KMS automatic rotation: KMS cannot rotate XKS keys itself (FAQ 'Can I rotate my keys': you manage rotation in your key manager).

claim: After you disable, block or delete an XKS key, the next API call fails for services that do not cache keys; services that cache data keys may keep them from 5 mins to 24 hrs, and resources in use react differently.
question: If you disable or delete an external key, where can data still be read in AWS?

values.display: the next API call using this XKS KMS key will fail

qualifiers.scope: per AWS service that caches data keys

evidence.quote: For services that do not cache keys, the next API call using this XKS KMS key will fail.
Caching of these keys can vary from 5 mins to 24 hrs.
Any protected resource that is currently in use (such as RDS database or EC2 instance) will respond differently after you deny access to the key.

claim: IAM policies, KMS key policies and grants work the same way for keys in external key stores as for other KMS keys; the XKS proxy can add a second layer of authorization.
question: How do you control access to XKS keys?

values.display: work the same way for KMS keys in external key stores

evidence.quote: All of the usual AWS KMS authorization mechanisms — IAM policies, AWS KMS key policies, grants — that you use with other KMS keys, work the same way for KMS keys in external key stores.

claim: With XKS you are responsible for the availability of the XKS Proxy and external key material; for example, if the proxy or key manager cannot decrypt an EBS volume key, the EC2 instance fails to launch.
question: What availability risk do you accept with an external key store?

values.display: responsible for the availability of the XKS Proxy
your EC2 instance will fail to launch

evidence.quote: Availability risk: You are responsible for the availability of the XKS Proxy and external key material.
If your XKS Proxy or external key manager isn’t available to decrypt the volume key, your EC2 instance will fail to launch.

claim: With XKS you alone are responsible for the durability of external keys; if the external key is permanently lost or deleted, all ciphertext encrypted under the XKS key is unrecoverable.
question: What happens if the external key behind an XKS key is lost?

evidence.quote: Durability risk: Because keys are under your control in systems outside of AWS, you are solely responsible for the durability of all external keys you create.
If the external key for a XKS key is permanently lost or deleted, all ciphertext encrypted under the XKS key is unrecoverable.

claim: If a single request from AWS KMS to the XKS Proxy, including one retry, takes more than 500ms, AWS KMS returns a 400 error to its caller; KMS retries once any request that takes 250ms.
question: What latency does AWS KMS tolerate from an XKS proxy?

qualifiers.scope: per request from AWS KMS to the XKS Proxy

evidence.quote: Also, if the elapsed time of a single request (including one retry) from AWS KMS to your XKS Proxy takes more than 500ms*, AWS KMS will return a 400 error to its calling client, effectively communicating that your XKS key is unavailable and the calling client should not retry.
*AWS KMS will attempt a single retry for any request that takes 250ms.

claim: Use of XKS is excluded from the public AWS KMS availability SLA, and XKS keys are also excluded from the availability SLA of any AWS service where you configure them to encrypt data.
question: Does the AWS KMS SLA cover external key stores?

values.display: specifically exclude the use of XKS

evidence.quote: Because AWS cannot control the end-to-end availability of the connection between AWS KMS and your external key store infrastructure, we specifically exclude the use of XKS in our public KMS availability SLA.
Also, XKS keys are excluded in the availability SLA for any AWS service in which an XKS key is configured by you to encrypt data within the service.

claim: You can temporarily disable KMS keys so that no one can use them, and re-enable them later.
question: Can you stop a KMS key from being used without deleting it?

evidence.quote: Temporarily disable keys so they cannot be used by anyone
